concepts.name: Chance and Probability
concepts.description: Probability is a mathematical measure of the likelihood of an event occurring. It provides a numerical value between 0 and 1, where 0 represents an impossible event and 1 represents a certain event.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the concept of probability and distinguish between impossible, possible, and certain events.

concepts.name: Random Experiments
concepts.description: A random experiment is an activity whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty in advance, even though all possible outcomes are known.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify random experiments and list their possible outcomes.

concepts.name: Experimental Probability
concepts.description: Experimental probability is determined by conducting an experiment and calculating the ratio of the number of times an event occurs to the total number of trials performed.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the experimental probability of an event using observed data.

concepts.name: Frequency and Relative Frequency
concepts.description: The frequency of an event is the number of times it occurs during an experiment, while relative frequency is the ratio of that frequency to the total number of trials.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to determine the frequency and relative frequency of events from experimental data.

concepts.name: Large Number of Trials
concepts.description: As the number of trials increases, the experimental probability generally approaches the theoretical probability, illustrating the long-term stability of probability.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain how increasing the number of trials affects the accuracy of experimental probability.

concepts.name: Equally Likely Outcomes
concepts.description: Theoretical probability is based on the assumption that all possible outcomes of an experiment are equally likely to occur.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify equally likely outcomes in simple probability experiments.

concepts.name: Probability Formula
concepts.description: The probability of an event is calculated using the formula: Probability = (Number of favourable outcomes) / (Total number of possible outcomes).
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to compute the theoretical probability of simple events using the standard formula.

concepts.name: Applications of Probability
concepts.description: Probability is applied in fields such as science, weather forecasting, insurance, finance, medicine, and decision-making to estimate uncertainty and risk.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve real-life problems involving theoretical probability.

concepts.name: Key Concepts of Probability
concepts.description: This chapter summarizes the concepts of random experiments, experimental probability, theoretical probability, and the relationship between observed and expected outcomes.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate and interpret probabilities of simple events and apply probability concepts to real-world situations.
